speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) whether there are plans to designate additional Silver Zones beyond the planned 50; (b) if yes, when is the next phase of implementation; and (c) if no, whether LTA will review the Silver Zone plans, given the needs of our continually ageing population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister of State for Transport)
text: Introduced in 2023, Friendly Streets encompass and build on existing efforts, such as Silver Zones.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First is, there was an 80% drop in traffic accidents involving senior pedestrians in Silver Zone areas.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Can I ask about the Friendly Streets pilot, whether it has also been effective in ensuring and improving safety of the neighbourhoods?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Second, in Nee Soon South, about one in three residents is a senior above 50 years old, but also at the same time, like Punggol, we have a growing young family population.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am happy to hear that Family Streets is the way forward to improve safety of the different neighbourhoods, catering to the different needs.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: And also, maybe, can I ask the friendly Senior Minister of State to consider Nee Soon South, to be included in the friendly list of the next batch of Friendly Streets?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Friendly Streets will be implemented in high-pedestrian flow, high-activity areas.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have received strong support and feedback from the residents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These were, for example, launched in Punggol just last weekend.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These are initiatives which will benefit both the elderly as well as young families.
